In Fairview, Vancouver, the 55+ homes you can buy are Terraces on 7th (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care and subsidized rental. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Fairview
Terraces on 7th (Terraces On Seventh) — 1570 West 7th Avenue (Fairview / South Granville)

The one verified age-restricted strata ownership building in Fairview — and a hybrid product: you buy a strata suite inside a building that also operates as a boutique retirement community. A current listing for a suite in the building states it outright: "Welcome to the Terraces on 7th, a much sought after retirement community with a 55 plus age restriction." The building-data source for the same address records that the strata bylaws include age restrictions (with pets allowed), that the building was built in 2003, and that it has 52 units, with elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access. SOURCE NOTE on the year: the listing text states "Built in 2002" while the building-data source states built in 2003 — treat the exact build year as 2002/2003, not confirmed to a single year.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Fairview (not for sale)

items.t: Broadway Lodge — 1377 Lameys Mill Road (False Creek South): The operator describes Broadway Lodge as a "114 bed complex care (long term care) home located in Vancouver's South False Creek area." A June 8, 2022 Council motion records the same figure and the building's singular position: Broadway Lodge "is the only long term care home in False Creek South or anywhere between Arbutus and Main and north of Broadway," it has provided care and housing for seniors in False Creek South for over 40 years, and it leases a parcel of City-owned land in False Creek South with the lease expiring in 2040. Care only — admission is through the long-term care system.
Glynn Manor — 520 West 7th Avenue: Non-profit, directory-listed — a few blocks west of Terraces on 7th on the same avenue.

Heather Place — 774 West 13th Avenue: Non-profit/BC Housing, directory-listed. (The separate Heather Place redevelopment project is in the Checked list below — it is mixed housing, not a seniors-only building.)
Magnolo Manor — 2675 Alder Street: Non-profit, directory-listed.
Cypress Walk — 2425 Cypress Street: BC Housing, directory-listed.
Seven Maples / Woodcroft — 1987 West 7th Avenue: BC Housing, directory-listed.
Strathearn Court — 1873 Spyglass Place (False Creek South): Non-profit, directory-listed.
Van Coevorden Court — 1099 Sitka Square (False Creek South): Non-profit, directory-listed.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Fairview

items.t: Fairview is the City of Vancouver's official local area name, one of its 22 distinct areas, on the south shore of False Creek, running from Granville Island along False Creek to Science World and south to Shaughnessy. The City page does not state a full set of boundary roads in text, and exact boundary roads are not verified from a City text source. The Broadway Plan area covering Fairview's northern part runs between Clark Drive and Vine Street and 1st and 16th Avenues.

Inside the local area sit False Creek South (the waterfront community on City-held leasehold land), the Fairview Slopes (under the FM-1 district), South Granville (the shopping district at the west side, with Gallery Row) and Granville Island.
West Broadway, Granville Street, Burrard Street, Cambie Street and West 2nd Avenue serve the area, with the Granville, Burrard and Cambie Street bridges crossing False Creek at its north edge.

Schools located in the area (VSB, SD39; catchments are address-based — check the VSB locator for any specific home): L'Ecole Bilingue Elementary, 1166 West 14th Avenue, and False Creek Elementary, 900 School Green, in False Creek South. A public secondary school located inside the local area: Not verified. SD39 has no middle-school tier (K–7 / 8–12).

Health care defines this area: Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, is inside the local area on the West Broadway corridor — the hospital a Fairview senior actually uses is in the neighbourhood, not across a bridge.

Library: Firehall Branch of Vancouver Public Library, 1455 West 10th Avenue. Parks and waterfront: Charleson Park, 999 Charleson Street, sits on the False Creek seawall in False Creek South, and the seawall runs the area's whole north edge. A community centre located inside the local area named on a City source: Not verified.

Transit: Broadway-City Hall Station (Canada Line) and Olympic Village Station (Canada Line) serve the area's east and north-east edges; the 99 B-Line runs via West Broadway from Commercial-Broadway Station to UBC and route 9 serves Broadway to Alma Street; route 50 runs via Granville Island to Olympic Village Station. The Broadway Subway — a 5.7-kilometre Millennium Line extension from VCC-Clark Station to Arbutus Street with six new stations, including South Granville and Broadway-City Hall — is on schedule to open in fall 2027, per the Province.

Where the 55+ housing actually is: one pocket — the West 7th Avenue / South Granville blocks, where Terraces on 7th (the area's one verified 55+ ownership building) stands at 1570 West 7th Avenue, with Glynn Manor, a subsidized seniors building, at 520 West 7th Avenue — plus False Creek South, where Broadway Lodge long-term care sits on Lameys Mill Road and the area's older population is concentrated.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Fairview

items.t: How the City creates new 55+ rental: Vancouver's Seniors Housing Rezoning Policy (approved July 23, 2024; last amended May 19, 2026) treats "Social Housing (where occupancy is restricted to older adults 55+)" as social housing secured by a housing agreement restricting occupancy to residents aged 55 or older, owned and operated by a non-profit or government, and secures seniors supportive or independent living housing as rental — no stratification, no separate sales — for 60 years or the life of the building.

Fairview Slopes zoning: FM-1 District Schedule of By-law No. 3575: — its stated intent is to enhance the small-scale residential character of the Fairview Slopes neighbourhood by encouraging retention of existing houses and permitting new low-profile residential development; FM-1 permits single detached houses, duplexes, multiple dwellings and multiple conversion dwellings at a maximum floor space ratio of 0.60, with no minimum site area stated in the schedule overview. Southern Fairview lots also fall under R1-1 (multiplex up to 6 units, or up to 8 rental units; a single detached house may include a secondary suite and a laneway house); C-3A covers the commercial mixed-use streets. Parcel-level zone: Not verified.
Tenure in False Creek South: Leasehold does not comp against freehold Fairview product.

The Broadway Plan and the subway: the Broadway Plan covers Fairview's northern half (Clark Drive to Vine Street, 1st to 16th Avenues) and the Broadway Subway is scheduled to open in fall 2027 — lots inside the plan area, including the West 7th Avenue blocks around Terraces, carry plan expectations the base zoning alone does not show.

Tax calendar: City of Vancouver 2026 advance taxes were due February 3, 2026 and main taxes July 3, 2026, with a 5% penalty after each due date; the Empty Homes Tax requires an annual property status declaration, with the 2025 payment due April 16, 2026.

blocks.text: The BC rules on 55+ age bylaws, who may own and who may live in a unit, the exemptions and rentals apply in every strata and are explained once, with sources, on the BC 55+ strata rules page.

items.t: BC 55+ strata rules

False Creek South is one of the oldest-skewing pockets in the city, and Council has the numbers: the June 8, 2022 Council motion records that in False Creek South nearly one in three residents are above the age of 65 — over 2,150 seniors (65 years and over), 35.9% of the area's population, up from 30.4% in the 2016 Census and more than double the 17% for the city as a whole — and that as residents age in place there are very few opportunities to move into appropriate "rightsized" housing. That demographic pressure is the backdrop for every seniors-housing decision in Fairview.

False Creek South's care future is being negotiated as a "Campus of Care": the same 2022 motion records that Broadway Lodge and the Residences for Independent Living Society have both provided care and housing in False Creek South for over 40 years, both lease City-owned land (leases expiring in 2036 and 2040), the Lodge's 114 beds will need substantial upgrading by 2030, and the two operators have joined together as the Broadway Group to propose a Campus of Care vision.

Terraces on 7th's build year is stated two ways in its own public record: the sale listing says "Built in 2002," the building-data source says built in 2003, and a 2003 provincial release records independent living units announced for "The Terraces on 7th Avenue, located at 1570 West 7th" — a one-year discrepancy to settle from the strata plan and depreciation report, not from marketing.

Heather Place is two different projects with one name: the existing Heather Place at 774 West 13th Avenue is a directory-listed seniors development, while the Heather Place redevelopment at 725–799 West 14th Avenue is a 230-home mixed project for families, seniors and people with disabilities replacing 86 aging units — citing the redevelopment's unit count as "seniors housing" overstates the seniors stock by design.

The West 7th Avenue pocket predates the Broadway Subway by two decades and will outlast its construction: Glynn Manor (520 West 7th) and Terraces on 7th (1570 West 7th) both sit on the avenue the Broadway Plan covers and the subway will serve from fall 2027 — the area's seniors stock is concentrated on exactly the corridor now being rebuilt around it, with the South Granville station at the pocket's west end.

On the Slopes, FM-1 — not the R1-1 multiplex rules — prices the lot: FM-1 caps floor space ratio at 0.60 and is written to retain existing houses and keep new development low-profile, so a multiplex pitch copied from a southern Fairview R1-1 street misprices a Slopes lot; the two zoning worlds sit blocks apart inside one small local area.

faq.a: One building: Terraces on 7th, 1570 West 7th Avenue — a 52-unit strata whose listing states a 55 plus age restriction and whose building data records age restrictions in the strata bylaws, operating as a boutique retirement community for independent living. Everything else verified in Fairview is subsidized rental or long-term care. Confirm the current bylaw wording and any mandatory services agreement in the strata documents before offering.
faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually buy in Fairview?

faq.a: Both halves are documented: suites in the building are listed for sale as strata units (MLS® is a sale listing), and the operator markets the same address as a retirement community for independent living with private suites. The ownership is strata; what the retirement-community operation adds — services, meals, any mandatory charge on top of strata fees — is not confirmed from public sources and is the first thing to verify in the disclosure and strata documents.
faq.q: Is Terraces on 7th a rental retirement home or a condo I own?

faq.a: They are non-profit seniors rentals in BC Housing's Zone 6 directory (May 2025), Fairview section — apply through BC Housing's Housing Registry or directly with the operator, and expect a waitlist. The City points seniors to the Seniors Services Society's Seniors Housing Directory of BC for the full list.
faq.q: How do I get into Glynn Manor or the other subsidized buildings?

faq.a: Inside the area: Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, on the West Broadway corridor — a few blocks from Terraces on 7th and the West 7th Avenue seniors pocket.

The in-area ladder is: independent strata living at Terraces on 7th (with its retirement-community operation), subsidized independent rental (Glynn Manor and the other directory buildings), then long-term care at Broadway Lodge in False Creek South — which the City records is the only long-term care home in False Creek South or anywhere between Arbutus and Main and north of Broadway.
faq.q: If I need care later, can I stay in Fairview?

faq.a: Both checks are mandatory there: False Creek South homes sit on City-held land under ground leases, and the City's False Creek floodplain includes False Creek South along Fairview's south shore, with Building By-law setback and flood construction level requirements for parcels in it. A specific building's lease terms and a specific parcel's floodplain status: Not verified — read the lease and check the parcel in the City dataset.
